## Timeout configuration & enforcement in httpx

**Configuration (data model):**
- `httpx/_config.py:72` — the `Timeout` class, holding `connect`/`read`/`write`/`pool` floats, with `__init__` parsing/normalizing the various input forms (single float, tuple, per-phase kwargs) and `.as_dict()` for serialization.
- `httpx/_client.py:196,212` — `BaseClient.__init__` accepts `timeout: TimeoutTypes = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_CONFIG` and stores it as `self._timeout = Timeout(timeout)`.
- `httpx/_client.py:254-259` — `timeout` property getter/setter on the client.
- Per-request overrides: every `request`/`get`/`post`/etc. method (`_client.py`, many call sites e.g. L352, L653, L785...) accepts its own `timeout: TimeoutTypes | UseClientDefault = USE_CLIENT_DEFAULT`, falling back to the client default when unset.

**Enforcement (where it actually bites):**
- `httpx/_client.py:371-377` and `httpx/_client.py:584-591` (`BaseClient._set_timeout`) — just before sending, httpx converts the resolved `Timeout` into a dict and stashes it in `request.extensions["timeout"]` if not already present.
- This `extensions["timeout"]` dict is passed down to the transport (`httpx/_transports/default.py`), which forwards it to **httpcore**'s connection pool/socket layer — httpcore is the library that actually starts timers and raises on expiry. httpx itself does no socket-level waiting.
- Timeout errors surface as `httpx/_exceptions.py`: `ConnectTimeout` (L140), `ReadTimeout` (L146), `WriteTimeout` (L152), `PoolTimeout` (L158), all subclassing `TimeoutException` (L132), which httpx re-raises from the underlying httpcore exceptions (mapped in `httpx/_transports/default.py::_load_httpcore_exceptions()`).

So: configuration lives entirely in `httpx/_config.py` and `httpx/_client.py`; actual timing/enforcement happens inside `httpcore` (an external dependency), with httpx only passing the timeout dict through extensions and translating resulting exceptions.
